why: A bitmask is a set: every integer mask from 0 to 2^n - 1 picks the elements whose bits are 1, so iterating masks in increasing order enumerates all subsets in exactly the order the judge asks for.
hints: How many subsets does a set of n elements have, and how could you number them?
Give each element a bit: bit i is 1 when nums[i] is in the subset. Masks 0..2^n-1 are exactly the subsets.
for mask in range(1 << n): append [nums[i] for i in range(n) if mask >> i & 1]. O(n * 2^n).
pitfalls: The empty subset (mask 0) must be included.
Inside each subset keep the original input order: loop i from 0 upwards.
Backtracking produces the subsets in a different order; this judge wants increasing mask order.
